mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption-led recession with a housing rebound, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to lower corporate profit margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), indicates weakening manufacturing and demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA AND RSAFS < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which typically precedes a risk-off shift and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 300,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously falls below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, accompanied by a rise in housing starts (HOUST), indicates a broad-based supply-side expansion, which tends to boost earnings expectations and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
